title: A Study of a New Induction and Dosing Schedule for Sublocade in Opioid Use Disorder
official: BRIDGE Study: Buprenorphine XR Real-world Induction, Dosing, and Gradual Evaluation
summary:
This study is looking at a new way to start Sublocade, a monthly injectable medicine already approved in Canada for opioid use disorder. Right now, most people start Sublocade with two doses of 300 mg, one month apart. This study is testing a different, more gradual approach: a smaller dose (50 mg) on Day 1, a second small dose (50 mg) on Day 7, and then the regular dose (300 mg) on Day 14.

The study team wants to find out whether this gradual approach helps people transitioning from methadone, or people who have used buprenorphine before, get started on treatment more easily. Everyone in the study follows the same schedule, and no one gets a placebo (an inactive treatment).

Participants will get study visits on Day 1, Day 7, and Day 14, along with short daily check-ins about how they're feeling for about 4 weeks, and some questionnaires about their quality of life and treatment satisfaction. The study is being done at one clinic in Calgary, Alberta.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Currently receiving methadone treatment, OR active opioid use disorder with prior exposure to buprenorphine
* Willingness and ability to provide informed consent to participate

Exclusion Criteria:

* No diagnosis of opioid use disorder and no prior buprenorphine exposure
* Known intolerance or hypersensitivity to buprenorphine
